title: REPORT on the implementation of the common security and defence policy – annual report 2025
part_text: 29. Expresses its dismay at the December 2025 US National Security Strategy, which formalises a groundless US policy of considering the EU, including its fundamental values, democratic governance principles and several of its fundamental security objectives, opposed to US interests; underscores that such positions inevitably lead European countries to reinforce their strategic autonomy, including in the EU-US defence and security relationship; acknowledges NATO’s crucial role for Europe’s collective defence, but warns of the risks posed by the growing unpredictability, short-sighted isolationism and self-centredness in US foreign policy and its shifting relations with Russia and focus on Asia, which could be accompanied by a stark decrease in military posture and the rapid withdrawal of troops from Europe and be perceived as undermining its security commitments to Europe; calls, against this backdrop, for the development of contingency plans in case of rapid US troop withdrawal, or as a result of any other circumstances, to ensure European deterrence and capacity for autonomous action against aggression;
